prompt:
I need the front end for Precedent. A searchable archive of an architecture firm's past projects, drawings and photos, used in-house to find earlier work to build on.

Who's using it: A group of four at a 60-person architecture firm's Monday pin-up review: principal Hana Lindqvist, project architect Owen Mbeki, and two junior designers. They're standing in front of the large wall display in the studio, and Owen is the one typing.

What they're doing right now: They're reviewing early concepts for a municipal parking structure, and Hana remembers the firm did a perforated-metal facade screen 'around 2018, maybe for a hospital garage'. The group needs to find that project and similar precedents quickly. They'll narrow by building type, material and year, compare a handful of candidates together, and pick two to pull detail drawings from while everyone is still in the room.

What's in the system at this point: Archive: 1,840 projects from 1994–2026, 64,300 drawings, 22,100 photos, 3,900 specification documents. Each project has a number (e.g., 2018-041), name, client, building type, city, completion year, project lead, materials tags, and awards. Likely candidates: 2018-041 'St. Brendan Medical Center Parking Expansion' (anodized aluminum perforated panels, 6 detail sheets), 2016-112 'Riverside Transit Garage' (expanded metal mesh), 2021-007 'Civic Arts Center Parking' (folded perforated steel, AIA regional award). 312 projects are tagged 'parking'. Related spec section 05 75 00 'Decorative formed metal' appears in 41 projects. The archive also suggests 'often referenced together' projects.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
